AUTHOR: Ditria
TITLE: Deep learning for automated analysis of fish abundance: the benefits of training across multiple habitats
REGION: Tweed River estuary, northern New South Wales, Australia
DATA: Own footage (submerged action cameras, Feb 2019–Mar 2020); three training sets (~4,700 annotations each: seagrass, reef, combination) and two test sets (48 videos each, ~1,500 annotations)
V_EV: Discussion: 'the water was often more turbid and picture clarity was thus affected (Figure 2)'; Methods: 'variability in other environmental factors such as lighting and water turbidity' — qualitative only
D2: ~4,700 annotations per training set; two test sets of 48 videos (~1,500 annotations) each
D_EV: Methods: 'The two test datasets... were comprised of video footage that did not appear in the training data (Figure 1)'
R_EV: Methods: footage 'deployed in the two most dissimilar habitats... seagrass meadows and rocky reefs, between February 2019 and March 2020, in the Tweed River estuary'
C_EV: no statement found (no confidence threshold; Table 1 FP counts are ordinary evaluation against ground truth)
E_EV: Methods: 'Fish abundance performance was tested using MaxN ... Performance on MaxN was calculated by an F1 score'; test annotations 'pre-annotated and used as the ground truth'
ARCH: Mask R-CNN (maskrcnn-benchmark, Massa & Girshick 2018) with ResNet50 backbone; early stopping
